headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and code-execution pair: default configs enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading unsafe actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and Gemini CLI also uses MCP plus stdin/stdout, so attacker-controlled files or shared workspace artifacts can be treated as instructions. Open Interpreter has clipboard and whole-filesystem access, increasing the chance it ingests Gemini-produced content. The pathway exists in default shared-workspace use, though not via a dedicated shared channel.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace or exchange files through the filesystem, prompt injection is possible.
IF Open Interpreter reads Gemini-generated files or clipboard content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer actions.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable clipboard-based handoff for Open Interpreter.
Require manual review of any file produced by the other agent.
Use a read-only export directory for cross-agent artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, shell environment, and can egress broadly; Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and also has broad network egress. In a shared workspace, sensitive local files can flow into either agent’s context and then out to external model providers. The blast radius includes secrets and local data exfiltration by default.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a directory containing secrets or private documents, those contents can be exposed to the other agent.
IF Open Interpreter or Gemini CLI sends retrieved file contents to configured model providers, local data can leave the machine.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate OS user account.
Restrict both agents to a minimal project directory.
Remove secrets from the shared workspace before use.
Disable network egress except to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state, while Gemini CLI shares state via filesystem and git and Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem. Concurrent writes to the same repo or directory can corrupt files, overwrite commits, or create conflicting git history. This is a default-dangerous overlap with irreversible repository damage potential.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, concurrent commits or file edits can conflict.
IF either agent runs without external locking, last-writer-wins overwrites are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate clone.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Disable automatic commits for one agent.
Review diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce code, file edits, and shell actions that Open Interpreter may then consume and act on, and Open Interpreter can execute arbitrary code as the invoking user. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious A output can cascade into destructive local actions. The pair’s default tool-use patterns make this a dangerous handoff.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is fed Gemini CLI output without verification, it may execute incorrect commands.
IF Gemini CLI generates file edits that Open Interpreter later runs as code, errors can cascade into local actions.
mitigations: Require human approval for every cross-agent action.
Insert a verification step before execution.
Use dry-run mode for both agents.
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only analysis when consuming Gemini output.
requires-engineering: build typed handoff contracts between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not state residency or certification constraints, so no specific breach is provable. However, Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and Gemini CLI can handle source code and shell environment, so compliance-sensitive data may be processed by both under unspecified retention and provider policies. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the local filesystem or workspace, both agents may process it.
IF configured model providers retain prompts or files, retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace.
Use provider settings with minimal retention.
Document data handling for both agents.
Run in a segregated environment for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
